paper.title_en: Direct mass measurement of <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Rh</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>91</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Ru</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>89</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and mid-shell trend of the one-proton separation energies for <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> nuclei
paper.abstract_en: Neutron-deficient nuclei in the <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≈</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>90</mn></mrow></math> region were produced by fragmentation of a relativistic <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Ag</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>107</mn></mmultiscripts></math> beam at the GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research (GSI), separated in the fragment separator FRS, slowed down, and thermalized, and high-precision mass measurements were performed employing the multiple-reflection time-of-flight mass spectrometer (MR-TOF-MS) of the FRS Ion Catcher. The masses of <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Rh</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>91</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>93</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>95</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Ru</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>89</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Tc</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>88</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Mo</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>87</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>88</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>89</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></math>, and <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Nb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>87</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>88</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>89</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></math> were determined. The mass of <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Rh</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>91</mn></mmultiscripts></math> was measured for the first time. For <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Ru</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>89</mn></mmultiscripts></math>, the measured mass excess deviates by more than ten standard deviations (361 keV) from the previous measurement. A possible misidentification of the measured nuclei, including <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Ru</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>89</mn></mmultiscripts></math>, with contaminants was excluded using a newly developed identification technique for MR-TOF-MS measurements. For the other nuclides, the measured masses agree well with previous measurements. The impact of the new masses on the one-proton separation energy (<math><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></math>) of the nuclei with constant total isospin projection (<math><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>z</mi></msub></math>) in the island of inversion around <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>40</mn></mrow></math> is investigated, and signatures of the deformed shell gap at <math><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>38</mn></mrow></math> are found. A comparison of the experimental <math><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></math> values with the predictions of several mass models shows a general agreement of the trends.
